title: DTOs & validation: the contract at the edge

questions.prompt: A handler is `create(@Body() dto: CreateOrderDto)` and the DTO's fields carry `@IsUUID()` / `@IsInt()`. A request with `quantity: "lots"` reaches the handler unvalidated. What's missing?

options.text: A ValidationPipe — nothing reads the decorators at runtime unless a pipe is registered
The DTO needs to be an interface instead of a class
A guard on the controller
`strict: true` in tsconfig

questions.explanation: TypeScript types are erased; the decorators only add metadata. `app.useGlobalPipes(new ValidationPipe(...))` (or `@UsePipes`) is the runtime component that reads that metadata, transforms the payload, and throws 400. It must be a class, not an interface, precisely because the metadata needs somewhere to live.

questions.prompt: Why is `whitelist: true` a security control rather than a tidiness setting?

options.text: Undeclared properties otherwise survive into the handler, and anything doing a bulk update writes them — mass assignment of fields like `role`
It rejects oversized payloads
It escapes HTML in string fields
It makes the DTO's TypeScript type exact

questions.explanation: `whitelist: true` deletes every property with no validation decorator, so `repo.update(id, dto)` can only write fields you declared. Without it the DTO documents a contract the pipe doesn't enforce. `forbidNonWhitelisted: true` is the stricter form: reject rather than strip.

questions.prompt: `@Query("page") page: number` receives `?page=2`. What is `page` at runtime?

options.text: The string "2" — the query string is text; the annotation doesn't convert it
The number 2; Nest reads the type annotation and converts
NaN, unless ParseIntPipe is applied
undefined, because query params need a DTO

questions.explanation: Params, query and headers are always strings on the wire, and the type annotation is erased — so you get a string typed as a number, which quietly breaks arithmetic and comparisons. Fix it with `ParseIntPipe`, or a query DTO with `@Type(() => Number)` and `transform: true`.

questions.prompt: `CreateCustomerDto` has an `address` object whose DTO carries decorators, but bad addresses are accepted. Which pair of decorators is required on the parent's field?

options.text: `@ValidateNested()` **and** `@Type(() => AddressDto)`
`@IsObject()` alone
`@ValidateNested()` alone
`@IsDefined()` plus `@IsNotEmptyObject()`

questions.explanation: `@ValidateNested()` tells class-validator to recurse; `@Type()` tells class-transformer to instantiate the nested class so its decorator metadata is actually found (and needs `transform: true`). Miss either one and the whole subtree is silently unvalidated — the most common validation hole in a Nest codebase.

questions.prompt: Signup must reject an email that's already registered. Where does that check belong, and what status?

options.text: In the service, as a 409 Conflict — backed by a unique index in the database
In a custom async validator on the DTO, as part of the 400
In a guard, as a 403
Nowhere — let the database's unique constraint surface as a 500

questions.explanation: The pipe's job is shape and syntax; "already taken" is a state-dependent invariant, so it belongs in the service with the status code that describes it. An async DB validator also races the write — only the unique index actually prevents the duplicate, so you need it regardless, and you catch its violation to return 409.

questions.prompt: Why derive the PATCH DTO with `class UpdateOrderDto extends PartialType(CreateOrderDto) {}` instead of writing it out?

options.text: It inherits every field and its constraints, adding `@IsOptional()` — so a rule added to create can't be forgotten on update
It's faster at runtime because metadata is shared
It makes all fields required, which PATCH needs
It's the only way to allow partial bodies

questions.explanation: Duplicated DTOs drift: someone tightens `@MaxLength` on create and PATCH silently keeps accepting the old input. `PartialType` (with `PickType`/`OmitType`/`IntersectionType`) keeps one source of truth. Note `@IsOptional()` means "may be absent" — not "may be null".

questions.prompt: Your user entity has `passwordHash`. What's the most robust way to keep it out of responses?

options.text: Return an explicit response object built field by field (a mapper) — impossible to break by forgetting a decorator
`@Exclude()` on the field plus ClassSerializerInterceptor — good, but silently leaks if the decorator is missed on a new field
`delete user.passwordHash` in the controller
Nothing — the request DTO already excludes it

questions.explanation: Both of the first two are real patterns; the mapper fails closed (a new field is invisible until you add it), while `@Exclude()` fails open (a new sensitive field leaks until someone decorates it). `delete` in the controller relies on every code path remembering, and the request DTO has nothing to do with the response shape.

prompts.prompt: Make validation the application-wide default: strip undeclared properties and return DTO instances with coerced types.
prompts.explanation: Registered globally, so the next controller someone adds is validated by default rather than by accident. `whitelist` strips undecorated properties (mass-assignment defence); `transform` gives the handler a real DTO instance and enables declared-type coercion.

prompts.prompt: Allow `note` to be absent, but cap its length when present.
prompts.explanation: `@IsOptional()` skips the remaining validators when the value is `undefined` — it does not permit `null`, and it isn't a substitute for a default. Without it, `@IsString()` fails on an absent field.

prompts.prompt: Validate a nested address object with its own DTO.
prompts.explanation: `@ValidateNested()` recurses into the object; `@Type(() => AddressDto)` converts the plain JSON into an `AddressDto` instance so its decorators are found. For an array, add `{ each: true }` to `@ValidateNested`.

prompts.prompt: Coerce a query-string page number into an actual number inside a query DTO.
prompts.explanation: Query values are always strings, so `@IsInt()` alone would reject `?page=2`. `@Type(() => Number)` converts before validation — explicit, and preferable to `enableImplicitConversion` when you want to know exactly which fields get coerced.

prompts.prompt: Derive the update DTO from the create DTO so every field becomes optional but keeps its constraints.
prompts.explanation: One source of truth for the contract. `PickType`, `OmitType` and `IntersectionType` cover the other shapes; hand-copying is how PATCH ends up accepting input that POST rejects.
